The economic effect of climate
 
Latitude is crucial to a nation’s strength, says Anjana Ahuja
 
(A) Dr William Masters was reading a book about mosquitoes when an idea struck him. ‘There was this anecdote about the yellow fever epidemic that hit Philadelphia in 1793,’ Masters recalls. ‘This epidemic decimated the city until the first frost came.’ The sub-zero temperatures froze out the insects, allowing Philadelphia to recover. If weather could be the key to a city’s fortunes, Masters thought, then why not to the historical fortunes of nations? And could frost lie at the heart of one of the most enduring economic mysteries of all – why are almost all the wealthy, industrialised nations to be found where the climate is cooler?
 
(B) After two years of research, he thinks that he has found a piece of the puzzle. Masters, an agricultural economist from Purdue University in Indiana, and Margaret McMillan at Tufts University, Boston, show that annual frosts are among the factors that distinguish rich nations from poor ones. Their study is published this month in the Journal of Economic Growth. The pair speculate that cold snaps have two main benefits – they freeze pests that would otherwise destroy crops, and also freeze organisms, such as those carried by mosquitoes, that carry disease. The result is agricultural abundance and a big workforce.
 
(C) The academics took two sets of information. The first was average income for countries, the second was climate data provided by the University of East Anglia. They found a curious tally between the sets. Countries having five or more frosty days in the winter months are uniformly rich; those with fewer than five are impoverished. The authors speculate that the five-day figure is important: it could be the minimum time needed to kill pests in the soil. To illustrate this, Masters notes: ‘Finland is a small country that is growing quickly, but Bolivia is a small country that isn’t growing at all. Perhaps climate has something to do with that.’
 
(D) Other minds have applied themselves to the split between poor and rich nations, citing anthropological, climatic and zoological reasons for why temperate nations are the most affluent. Jared Diamond, from the University of California at Los Angeles, pointed out in his book Guns, Germs and Steel that Eurasia is broadly aligned east-west, while Africa and the Americas are aligned north-south. So in Europe crops could move quickly across latitudes because climates are similar. One of the first domesticated crops, einkorn wheat, extended quickly from the Middle East into Europe; it took twice as long for it to get from Mexico to what is now the eastern United States. This easy movement along similar latitudes in Eurasia would also have meant a faster dissemination of other technologies, such as the wheel and writing, Diamond speculates.
 
(E) There are exceptions to the ‘cold equals rich’ argument. There are well-heeled tropical countries such as Singapore, a result of its superior trading position. Likewise, not all European countries are moneyed. Masters stresses that climate will never be the overriding factor – the wealth of nations is too complicated to be attributable to just one factor. Climate, he feels, somehow combines with other factors – such as the presence of institutions, including governments, and access to trading routes – to determine whether a country will do well.
 
(F) In the past, Masters says, economists thought that institutions had the biggest effect on the economy, because they brought order to a country in the form of, for example, laws and property rights. With order, so the thinking went, came affluence. ‘But there are some problems that even countries with institutions have not been able to get around,’ he says. ‘My feeling is that, as countries get richer, they get better institutions. And the accumulation of wealth and improvement in governing institutions are both helped by a favourable environment, including climate.’
 
(G) This does not mean, he insists, that tropical countries are beyond economic help and destined to remain penniless. Instead of aid being geared towards improving administrative systems, it should be spent on technology to improve agriculture and to combat disease. Masters cites one example: ‘There are regions in India that have been provided with irrigation – agricultural productivity has gone up and there has been an improvement in health.’ Supplying vaccines against tropical diseases and developing crop varieties that can grow in the tropics would break the poverty cycle.

Q14

干扰 你可能看到“yellow fever epidemic”想选疾病或疫苗，但这只是引发他思考的一个小故事，重点在于“an idea struck him”这个研究的起点。

句子 A段："Dr William Masters was reading a book about mosquitoes when an idea struck him. ... If weather could be the key to a city's fortunes, Masters thought, then why not to the historical fortunes of nations?"

解析 这一段讲马斯特斯在读书时突然有了一个想法，这就是他开始探究气候与国家命运关联这项研究的“灵感来源（inspiration）”。

Q15

解析 这段明确列举了寒冷天气（cold weather）带来的两大“好处（benefits/advantages）”：冻死害虫保护农业（agriculture），冻死带病生物保护人类（people）。

干扰 你可能看到“rich nations from poor ones”想选财富水平，但本段核心是在解释为什么冷的地方富，具体原因就是寒冷带来的实际“好处（advantages）”。

句子 B段："The pair speculate that cold snaps have two main benefits - they freeze pests that would otherwise destroy crops, and also freeze organisms, such as those carried by mosquitoes, that carry disease. The result is agricultural abundance and a big workforce."

Q16

解析 这段通过数据对比发现，霜冻天数多的国家富，天数少的国家穷，这直接证明了气候与经济之间存在“正相关关系（Positive correlations）”。

干扰 你可能看到芬兰和玻利维亚这两个小国就想选 iii（小国经历的问题），但这俩只是用来举例说明前面的气候规律，并非探讨小国特有的问题。

句子 C段："They found a curious tally between the sets. Countries having five or more frosty days in the winter months are uniformly rich; those with fewer than five are impoverished."

Q17

干扰 你可能看到“poor and rich nations”想选跟财富有关的选项，但整个大段的主体都在用单粒小麦等例子对比“不同大陆的传播速度”。

解析 这段的核心在对比地理走向导致的结果，即农作物（Crop）在欧洲（Europe）传播得很快，而在美洲等其他大陆（other continents）传播得很慢。

句子 D段："So in Europe crops could move quickly across latitudes because climates are similar. One of the first domesticated crops, einkorn wheat, extended quickly from the Middle East into Europe; it took twice as long for it to get from Mexico to what is now the eastern United States."

Q18

解析 这段强调财富水平（Levels of wealth）太复杂，不能只看气候，还受到诸如制度、政府、贸易路线等“其他多种因素（several other influences）”的综合影响。

干扰 你可能看到“governments”就想选 iv（政府在创造财富中的作用），但这里政府只是作为“其他因素”中的一个附属例子，中心思想是“除了气候还有别的因素”。

句子 E段："Masters stresses that climate will never be the overriding factor - the wealth of nations is too complicated to be attributable to just one factor. Climate, he feels, somehow combines with other factors - such as the presence of institutions, including governments, and access to trading routes - to determine whether a country will do well."

Q19

解析 这段先给出了过去经济学家的旧观念（有好制度才有钱），随后提出了作者的新感觉（有钱了才会有好制度），这就是对“传统观点（traditional view）”的反思。

干扰 你可能会因为看到“institutions”和“laws and property rights”去选其他干扰项，但必须注意句首的“In the past”和后文的“My feeling is...”，强调的是观点视角的转换。

句子 F段："In the past, Masters says, economists thought that institutions had the biggest effect on the economy... With order, so the thinking went, came affluence. ... 'My feeling is that, as countries get richer, they get better institutions.'"

Q20

句子 G段："Instead of aid being geared towards improving administrative systems, it should be spent on technology to improve agriculture and to combat disease. ... Supplying vaccines against tropical diseases and developing crop varieties... would break the poverty cycle."

干扰 你可能看到“vaccines”想选 ii（疫苗项目的失败），但原文是建议去“提供疫苗”，完全没说疫苗项目失败了，千万别无中生有。

解析 这段明确给出了建议，即资金援助（financial assistance = aid）不该花在行政系统上，而是最应该花在（best use = should be spent on）农业和疾病防治上。

Q21

解析 题目问费城在气温骤降时从什么当中恢复（recovered from its...），原文明确说是气温下降冻死昆虫让城市从“黄热病疫情（yellow fever epidemic）”中恢复过来。

干扰 你可能只想填“epidemic”，但在不超过三个词的限制下，连同具体的疾病名称（yellow fever epidemic）一起填上才是最完整准确的。

句子 A段："'There was this anecdote about the yellow fever epidemic that hit Philadelphia in 1793,' Masters recalls. 'This epidemic decimated the city until the first frost came.' The sub-zero temperatures froze out the insects, allowing Philadelphia to recover."

Q22

解析 题目要求填一个经济正在扩张（expanding = growing quickly）的小国例子，原文直接点名是“芬兰（Finland）”。

干扰 千万别填成了“Bolivia”（玻利维亚），原文明确说玻利维亚是根本没有增长（isn't growing at all）的反面例子。

句子 C段："To illustrate this, Masters notes: 'Finland is a small country that is growing quickly, but Bolivia is a small country that isn't growing at all.'"

Q23

句子 不要单填“wheat”或者“crops”，要写出原文中特指的完整作物名称 einkorn wheat。

解析 D段："One of the first domesticated crops, einkorn wheat, extended quickly from the Middle East into Europe; it took twice as long for it to get from Mexico to what is now the eastern United States."

干扰 题目问什么东西从墨西哥传播的速度比从中东传播要慢，原文通过比较说明这个作物就是“单粒小麦（einkorn wheat）”。

Q24

解析 你可能看到前面一句话有“Europe”想填欧洲，但包含“技术传播更快”这句话的主语明确限定的是“Eurasia”（欧亚大陆）。

干扰 题目问技术在哪里传播得比在非洲快，原文说“欧亚大陆（Eurasia）”的地理走向使得技术传播更快（faster dissemination = spread more quickly），并拿来与南北走向的非洲作了对比。

句子 D段："...Jared Diamond... pointed out... that Eurasia is broadly aligned east-west, while Africa and the Americas are aligned north-south. ... This easy movement along similar latitudes in Eurasia would also have meant a faster dissemination of other technologies, such as the wheel and writing..."

Q25

解析 题目问哪个国家尽管是热带气候但在经济上很富有（economically rich = well-heeled），原文给出的具体例外国家就是“新加坡（Singapore）”。

干扰 只要认出“well-heeled”是富有的意思，直接把后面的例子 Singapore 抄上即可。

句子 E段："There are well-heeled tropical countries such as Singapore, a result of its superior trading position."

Q26

解析 题目问援助应该用来改善农业，而不是（rather than）改善什么，原文对应的 instead of 后面跟着的拒绝选项是“行政系统（administrative systems）”。

干扰 别自己脑补成“government”，一定要紧扣原文中被“Instead of”直接否定的原词 administrative systems。

句子 G段："Instead of aid being geared towards improving administrative systems, it should be spent on technology to improve agriculture and to combat disease."
